items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: a Monsieur Souplet whom I had known for a long time

ctx.x: Juan-les-Pins had become very well known for its annual jazz festival. It was the second year that the festival was presented and the orchestras of Ray Charles and Count Basie were the big attractions. It was also the first time for Ray to play in Europe and the first time I ever heard him and saw him. He had a small group with two trumpets, three sax, bass and drums and the Raylettes. He sent me with his style of playing and singing and the arrangements were swinging like mad.

As I was already in Juan-le -Pins, one of the organisers, of the festival, a Monsieur Souplet whom I had known for a long time, wanted me to play one evening at the festival. He told me that there was going to be a very good trio playing that week and he thought that it would be an ideal group to accompany me. It was the trio of the pianist Les McCann. Eventually I met Les and mentioned to him that Souplet told me that he and I would play a set together the last night of the festival. He seemed to be for the…

Those days passed and he didn't contact me the day after. Then I began to get the feeling that this monkey didn't want to accompany me but wouldn't say it. I even told Souplet about my suspicion but he told me not to worry, that McCann had a stipulation in his contract about accompany another guest artist and everything would be OK.
